posts.title: How to sell assets on the Unity Asset Store (what we wish we'd known)
posts.seoTitle: How to Sell Assets on the Unity Asset Store: A Publisher's Guide
posts.description: A publisher's walkthrough of selling on the Unity Asset Store: the 70/30 split, the $4.99 minimum, key image sizes, packaging, review, pricing and the mistakes we made with 25+ packs.
posts.excerpt: The real path from a folder on your drive to a live listing: publisher profile, packaging, the four key images, review, pricing, and the things that tripped us up along the way.
posts.heroAlt: Arrow Escape cover art: a Unity arrow puzzle game template by Game Seed Assets
posts.heroCaption: Arrow Escape, one of our Unity templates. It went from project folder to live listing using the steps in this post.
keywords: sell assets on Unity Asset Store

posts.title: How to market your game assets when nobody knows your name yet
posts.seoTitle: How to Market Game Assets: What Works for a Small Publisher
posts.description: Practical marketing for Unity and Unreal asset creators: store pages that convert, free assets as a funnel, YouTube tutorials, Discord support, your own site, and what we'd skip.
posts.excerpt: A listing on a store with 12,000+ publishers is not a marketing plan. Here's what has actually moved things for us, with our own numbers, and what we'd skip.
posts.heroAlt: Dark 2D World Extended, a Limbo-style 2D environment pack for Unity
posts.heroCaption: Dark 2D World Extended. Its free little sibling does a lot of the marketing for it, as you'll see below.

posts.title: Reddit for Unity Asset Store creators: where to post, and how not to get removed
posts.seoTitle: Reddit for Unity Asset Store Creators: Subreddits, Rules and Posts
posts.description: Which subreddits suit Unity asset creators, what their self-promotion rules actually say, and how to post clips, free packs and breakdowns without getting removed or ignored.
posts.excerpt: Reddit is where Unity developers hang out when they're not working. It's also very good at smelling an ad. A subreddit-by-subreddit guide for asset creators.
posts.heroAlt: Free Fog Particles for Unity by Game Seed Assets
posts.heroCaption: Free packs like our Fog Particles are the easiest thing to share on Reddit, because the post gives something away instead of asking for something.

posts.title: Unity Asset Store vs Fab vs itch.io: where should you sell your game assets?
posts.seoTitle: Unity Asset Store vs Fab vs itch.io for Selling Game Assets
posts.description: Revenue split, audience, pricing rules, licences, payouts and upload effort compared for the Unity Asset Store (70/30), Fab (88/12) and itch.io (open revenue share), from a publisher on all three.
posts.excerpt: 70/30, 88/12, or whatever you choose on itch.io. The split is only one part of it. A side-by-side from a studio that sells on all three.
posts.heroAlt: Paper Plane Controller, sold on Fab with Unreal Engine and Unity versions
posts.heroCaption: Paper Plane Controller ships Unreal and Unity versions in one Fab listing, which is one of the things Fab does that the others don't.

posts.title: Key images, screenshots and trailers that sell Unity assets
posts.seoTitle: Unity Asset Store Key Images, Screenshots and Trailers That Sell
posts.description: The four Unity Asset Store key image sizes and their rules, how to design a card that reads at 420 pixels, captioned screenshots, and a 45-60 second trailer plan, using our own store media.
posts.excerpt: Buyers decide from a 420-pixel card and the first few seconds of a video. Our actual covers, cards, captioned screenshots and trailer plans, and the rules Unity enforces.
posts.heroAlt: Grass Cutting Simulator cover image, 1950 by 1300 pixels, by Game Seed Assets
posts.heroCaption: The Grass Cutting Simulator cover. We'll take it apart below, along with its card, icon and screenshots.
keywords: Unity Asset Store cover image size
